facts.statement: Sapeornis lived during the early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 to 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: Sapeornis is a monotypic genus of avialan dinosaurs which lived during the early Cretaceous period (late Barremian to early Aptian, roughly 125-120 mya).

facts.statement: Sapeornis was about 30 to 33 centimeters long when alive, excluding its tail feathers.
facts.quote: Sapeornis was large for an early avialan, about 30 - 33 cm long in life, excluding the tail feathers.

facts.statement: The skull of Sapeornis had only a few teeth located at the tip of the upper jaw.
facts.quote: The skull has a handful of teeth in the upper jawtip only.

facts.statement: A specimen of Sapeornis contained numerous small gastroliths in its stomach.
facts.quote: In specimen IVPP V12375, the stomach contained numerous small gastroliths.

facts.statement: Analysis of skeletal bones suggests Sapeornis had slow growth similar to Archaeopteryx, unlike the rapid growth of modern birds.
facts.quote: Analysis of its skeletal bones suggest that it had an ontogeny and slow growth like Archaeopteryx and small carnivorous dinosaurs, rather than the explosively fast growth seen in modern birds.

facts.statement: Sapeornis was likely a glider or soarer that preferred open country but could perch on branches.
facts.quote: Not being well-adapted to flapping flight, Sapeornis probably was a glider and/or soarer that preferred more open country compared to the Enantiornithes and predominantly woodland birds, although it was able to perch on branches.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Sapeornis was likely a herbivore that ate plant seeds and fruits.
facts.quote: The small gastroliths, overall large size, and the inferred habitat indicate that Sapeornis was most likely a herbivore, possibly eating plant seeds and fruits.

facts.statement: The first specimen of Sapeornis was found in the summer of 2000 near Chaoyang City, Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: The first known specimen (the type specimen) of Sapeornis was an incomplete skeleton dug up from Jiufotang Formation rocks in the area of Shangheshou, near Chaoyang City in Liaoning Province, China in the summer of 2000.

facts.statement: Sapeornis was discovered by the IVPP and reported in 2002 by scientists Zhonghe Zhou and Fucheng Zhang.
facts.quote: It was discovered by a team from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP), and was reported in 2002 by the scientists Zhonghe Zhou and Fucheng Zhang.

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Society of Avian Paleontology and Evolution combined with the Greek word for bird.
facts.quote: They chose the name in honor of SAPE, the Society of Avian Paleontology and Evolution, which they combined with the Ancient Greek word όρνις (ornis), meaning "bird".

facts.statement: Two more nearly complete specimens were found about 40 km from the original site in the Dapingfang area.
facts.quote: Soon after this, two more, nearly complete specimens were discovered in the Dapingfang area, about 40 km from the original fossil site.

facts.statement: A 2012 study concluded that Didactylornis, Shenshiornis, and S. angustis are synonyms of Sapeornis chaoyangensis.
facts.quote: In a 2012 study, Gao et al. concluded that Didactylornis was indeed a junior synonym of Sapeornis chaoyangensis, as were Shenshiornis and the supposed second species of Sapeornis, S. angustis.

facts.statement: Sapeornis belongs to the order Omnivoropterygiformes.
facts.quote: ordo: Omnivoropterygiformes

facts.statement: Sapeornis belongs to the family Omnivoropterygidae.
facts.quote: familia: Omnivoropterygidae

facts.statement: Sapeornis is classified within the class Aves.
facts.quote: classis: Aves

facts.statement: Sapeornis had tail feathers that formed a graded, fan-like structure.
facts.quote: The tail plumage of Sapeornis consisted of rectrices that formed a graded, fan-like structure.

facts.statement: The humerus of Sapeornis was large and had holes to save weight, similar to Confuciusornithidae.
facts.quote: The humerus was large and bore holes, apparently to save weight, as in the Confuciusornithidae.

facts.statement: Sapeornis had a rod-like pygostyle and lacked a long bony tail.
facts.quote: The pygostyle was rod-like as in Confuciusornis and Nomingia, but like in the former there was no long bony tail anymore.

facts.statement: The first toe of Sapeornis pointed backwards.
facts.quote: The first toe pointed backwards.

facts.statement: The reduced fingers of Sapeornis suggest it may have had an alula.
facts.quote: The reduced fingers suggest that it might have had an alula.

facts.statement: Character analysis demonstrates that Sapeornis was not closely related to Confuciusornis despite sharing some derived features.
facts.quote: However, the apomorphies were largely different from Confuciusornis, and a character analysis demonstrates that these two were not closely related.

facts.statement: Sapeornis measured between 30 and 33 centimeters in length, excluding the tail feathers which are unknown.
facts.quote: Este animal medía entre 30–33 centímetros de largo, excluyendo las plumas de la cola (las cuales son desconocidas).

facts.statement: Sapeornis possessed a hand far more advanced than Archaeopteryx, featuring three fingers with the outer one having two phalanges and the middle one having three, along with a carpometacarpus.
facts.quote: La mano de Sapeornis era de lejos más avanzada que la de Archaeopteryx. Tenía tres dedos, el más externo con dos falanges y el del medio tenía tres, y un carpometacarpo.

facts.statement: Sapeornis had arms one and a half times longer than its legs, suggesting a large wing area.
facts.quote: Sus brazos eran una vez y media más largos que sus patas, lo que sugiere una área alar grande.

facts.statement: The humerus of Sapeornis was large and contained holes, apparently to reduce weight, similar to Confuciusornithidae.
facts.quote: El húmero era grande y tenía agujeros, aparentemente para reducir el peso, como en las Confuciusornithidae.

facts.statement: The skull of Sapeornis had only a few teeth restricted to the anterior part of the mouth.
facts.quote: El cráneo solo tenía algunos dientes restringidos a la zona anterior de la boca.

facts.statement: Sapeornis possessed gastralia but lacked uncinate processes (or they were not ossified).
facts.quote: Sapeornis tenía gastralia pero sin procesos uncinados (o son osificar).

facts.statement: In specimen IVPP V12375, the stomach area contained numerous gastroliths.
facts.quote: En el espécimen IVPP V12375, la zona estomacal contiene numerosos gastrolitos.

facts.statement: Bone analyses indicate Sapeornis had slow ontogeny growth similar to Archaeopteryx and small carnivorous dinosaurs, rather than the rapid growth seen in modern birds.
facts.quote: Los análisis de sus huesos indican que su ontogenia era de crecimiento lento igual que en Archaeopteryx y los dinosaurios carnívoros pequeños, en lugar del crecimiento rápido visto en las aves modernas.

facts.statement: Considering absolute numbers of shared traits with modern birds, S. chaoyangensis was as advanced as Confuciusornis.
facts.quote: Considerando en números absolutos los rasgos compartidos por S. chaoyangensis con las aves modernas, este era tan avanzado como Confuciusornis.

facts.statement: Inferred from the slender pygostyle, Sapeornis likely had short tail feathers like Enantiornithes and Confuciusornis, with two to four long feathers on the tail.
facts.quote: Como se infiere del delgado pigóstilo, su plumaje caudal era probablemente corto como en las Enantiornithes y Confuciusornis, con entre dos a cuatro largas plumas en la cola.

facts.statement: Long feathers on the lower limbs were found in some specimens, giving them "four wings," a feature also found in Confuciusornis, Cathayornis, and Yanornis.
facts.quote: En algunos ejemplares se han encontrado plumas largas en las extremidades inferiores, teniendo por tanto "cuatro alas"; lo mismo se ha encontrado en ejemplares de Confuciusornis, Cathayornis y Yanornis.

facts.statement: Comparisons of sclerotic rings suggest Sapeornis may have been diurnal, like many modern birds.
facts.quote: Las comparaciones entre los anillos escleróticos de Sapeornis y aves y reptiles modernos indican que puede haber sido diurno, igual que muchas aves actuales.

facts.statement: Not well adapted for flapping flight, Sapeornis was likely a glider preferring open environments, though capable of perching on branches.
facts.quote: No estando bien adaptado al vuelo batiente, probablemente Sapeornis era un planeador que prefería ambientes más abiertos que los de las Enantiornithes y otras aves de zonas predominantemente arboladas, aunque era capaz de posarse en las ramas.

facts.statement: Small gastroliths and inferred habitat indicate Sapeornis was likely a herbivore, possibly feeding on seeds and fruits.
facts.quote: Los pequeños gastrolitos, y su hábitat inferido indican que Sapeornis era probablemente un herbívoro, posiblemente alimentándose de semillas y frutas.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence presented by Wang et al. (2026) shows Sapeornis utilized diverse food resources, including feeding on fruits.
facts.quote: Fossil evidence of utilization of diverse food resources by Sapeornis, including feeding on fruits, is presented by Wang et al. (2026).

facts.statement: In 2008, Yuan named a new specimen related to Sapeornis as Didactylornis jii.
facts.quote: En 2008, Yuan nombró a un nuevo espécimen relacionado con Sapeornis como Didactylornis jii.

facts.statement: In a 2012 study, Gao et al. reaffirmed that Didactylornis is the most modern synonym of Sapeornis chaoyangensis, as well as Shenshiornis and the supposed second species S. angustis.
facts.quote: En un estudio de 2012, Gao et al. reafirmaron que Didactylornis era ciertamente el sinónimo más moderno de Sapeornis chaoyangensis, así como Shenshiornis y la supuesta segunda especie de Sapeornis, S. angustis.

facts.statement: Omnivoropteryx is probably also another synonym of Sapeornis.
facts.quote: Omnivoropteryx es probablemente también otro sinónimo de Sapeornis.

facts.statement: Sapeornis lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sapeornis belongs to the parent group Pygostylia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Pygostylia

rejected.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings indicate Sapeornis may have been diurnal, similar to most modern birds.
rejected.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings of Sapeornis and modern birds and reptiles indicate that it may have been diurnal, similar to most modern birds.

rejected.statement: The first three specimens lacked feather traces but were recognized as the largest early Cretaceous avialans known at the time.
rejected.quote: None of these first three specimens preserved traces of feathers, but based on the size of their skeletons alone, they were recognized as the largest early Cretaceous avialans known at the time.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'were recognized as the largest early Cretaceous avialans'
